pattern_id: Commit-first dependency amnesia on unknown instances
description: In EPaxos, handleCommit installs a new instance when it receives a Commit for an (replica,instance) pair it has never seen (inst == nil) by blindly trusting the Seq and Deps carried in the Commit, without re-running local conflict detection. If the leader that issued the Commit has already forgotten some earlier conflicting instance A (e.g., due to crash-window or non-durable dependency index issues), then the Commit for B can carry a truncated dependency set that omits A. When a follower that *does* know about A receives this Commit first for B, handleCommit will create B with missing dependency on A instead of conservatively adding it. This leads to replicas that both have COMMITTED B but disagree on B's dependency set with respect to A. Because EPaxos Exec engine only uses metadata to order conflicting commands and does not attempt repair on EXECUTED instances, some replicas may execute A then B while others execute B then A, producing permanently divergent final application state.
fault_type: crash + message reordering (leader forgets dependency before Commit)
trigger_condition: 1) There exist two conflicting commands A and B on the same key. 2) A is committed earlier at (replicaA,instanceA) on some replicas, but the eventual leader for B has lost the in-memory conflict index for A (e.g., after crash+restart) and computes B's dependencies without including A. 3) The leader for B broadcasts a Commit(B) with truncated Deps that omit A. 4) A follower that has A in its log but no prior state for B (inst == nil) receives Commit(B) before any PreAccept/Accept/Prepare messages for B, so handleCommit installs B using only the Commit metadata and does not call updateAttributes. 5) Other replicas learn B via normal PreAccept/Accept or recovery and record B with Deps including A. 6) All replicas eventually COMMIT and EXECUTE both A and B using Exec, with some ordering A->B and others B->A, leading to divergent final state.
test_template: 1) Build an in-memory cluster using the repo's Replica test helper (e.g., CrashReuseReplica or equivalent) so you can directly manipulate InstanceSpace and run exec.executeCommand. 2) Construct a conflicting command A at instance (replicaA,instanceA) and mark it COMMITTED on all replicas, with no dependencies. 3) For command B at (replicaB,instanceB), install COMMITTED instances on a subset of replicas (e.g., R0,R1) with Seq_B > Seq_A and Deps_B[replicaA] = instanceA, as if they learned B through correct PreAccept/Accept or recovery that detected the conflict with A. 4) On another replica R2 that already has A but no prior state for B, call the real handleCommit with a Commit message whose Seq_B_truncated and Deps_B_truncated omit A, ensuring InstanceSpace[replicaB][instanceB] is nil before the call so you exercise the inst==nil branch. 5) Assert that after this, all replicas have B in Status=COMMITTED but with inconsistent (Seq,Deps) metadata (e.g., R0,R1 show B depends on A while R2 does not). 6) Drive the real Exec engine by calling exec.executeCommand(replicaB,instanceB) and exec.executeCommand(replicaA,instanceA) on all replicas in the same order. 7) Read the final value of the shared key on each replica and assert that at least two replicas disagree (e.g., some have x=2 and others x=1), and that no subsequent calls to executeCommand reorder or repair the divergence. This pattern can be adapted to other consensus implementations by replacing EPaxos-specific helpers with equivalent commit and execution paths, but the core idea is always: deliver a Commit-first for an unknown instance with truncated dependencies and check for divergent dependency metadata and final state across replicas.
